summary: The tower-defense example's own monitor: play it under a policy (a checkpoint and a threshold) and report finished, needs attention or inconclusive, with the evidence.

tools.name: monitor
tools.summary: Play tower defense in a running Workshop -- or watch it being played -- and say whether play went as the policy wants: FINISHED, NEEDS ATTENTION (more enemies crossed the checkpoint than the threshold allows, or the game was lost) or INCONCLUSIVE, with the evidence.
tools.description: Subscribes to the game's own publications (td.game's TdSeen and TdOccurred, through Workshop's observation relay) before anything is pressed, then prepares and plays: its own r begins a new game -- the game occurrence that press caused names this run's game -- each round's towers are pressed onto their cells and confirmed by the game's own tower occurrence caused by the presses, space begins the wave (confirmed the same way), and the run waits for the game to say the wave was held, won or lost. Every observation passes through the policy first: each enemy step onto the checkpoint cell is one crossing, and more than `threshold` crossings in this game NEEDS ATTENTION at once, whatever the run was waiting for. Then on_attention=pause presses p through this run's own input session and counts the pause done only when the game's TdSeen caused by that press says paused; the game is left paused. A win is FINISHED only when the pane's header agrees with the game's own numbers. A loss the relay or this client reports, a hole in the game's own numbering, the producer replaced, the observation ended, a wait or the monitor's own deadline run out: INCONCLUSIVE -- never a finish. plan=watch presses nothing and follows the game being played; crossings said before it joined are unknown, so its finish under the threshold is INCONCLUSIVE. build=frontier (or build, load-built) runs the Builder first, followed through its own words as workshop/builder does; without it the game must already run here, and a monitor that finds nobody holding td.game fails at once saying so. The run passes when the outcome is the one `expect` names.

inputs.name: plan
inputs.help: win or thin (plans.json beside the policy), or watch: press nothing, follow the game being played

inputs.name: checkpoint
inputs.help: the road cell x,y whose crossings are counted

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.help: the most crossings of the checkpoint one game may have; one more needs attention

inputs.name: on_attention
inputs.help: pause (press p, confirmed by the game's own word) or report (act on nothing)

inputs.name: expect
inputs.help: finished, needs-attention or any: which outcome passes the run

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.help: the monitor's own deadline: running out is INCONCLUSIVE, never the game's failure

inputs.name: build
inputs.help: empty: the game must already run here (the prerequisite); frontier, build or load-built: that Builder act first

inputs.name: recipe
inputs.help: the recipe a build act chooses

inputs.name: pictures
inputs.help: also keep last-wave.png (when the last wave's tenth enemy enters) and won.png

inputs.name: pace_ms
inputs.help: a pause after each gesture, so a person can watch; what decides is unchanged

outputs.name: monitor.json
outputs.help: the outcome and why; the policy's summary (checkpoint, threshold, this run's game, every crossing with its occurrence number, wave, tick and the far host's history numbers); the subscription and the producer's identity; every observation kept; the triggering ones; the newest TdSeen; each gesture and what confirmed it; the intervention; detection latency and phase times

outputs.name: attention.png
outputs.help: on attention: a picture of Workshop (attention.cells.txt in a terminal medium), with attention-rows.json, the game pane's rows

outputs.name: won.json
outputs.help: on a win: the game pane's rows the finish was checked against

outputs.name: build.json
outputs.help: with build: the Builder's own account, as workshop/builder's builder.json

requires: a Workshop guest granting input and capture whose row may observe td.game's TdSeen v1 and TdOccurred v1 (and zengine.builder's BuildAsked v1 and BuildStatus v4 to build)
the game pane open where Workshop describes it (td.game loaded under that role), unless build loads it
zengine-guest-vocabulary booted in this Loom session, and the workshop package approved beside this one
no other run on this link holding Workshop's input session (plan=watch holds none until it pauses)
tools.example: loom-session run <dir> tower-defense/monitor --name td-thin --input plan=thin --input expect=needs-attention --wait 600
tools.recovery: Read monitor.json: `words` says why, `trigger` holds the observations that decided it, `policy.crossings` every crossing counted. A wait that ran out leaves the run to its manager: wait for or show it again by name; cancelling it releases its subscription and its input session (its cleanup) and stops nothing the game is doing. INCONCLUSIVE names what could not be told. A refused subscription means the guest's row may not observe td.game: the maker adds it to the guests file's observe list. A refused pause means the guest has no input power: the attention stands, and nothing was done to the game.
